sentences.en: Hello, my name's Nicholas Davidoff, and in 2015, I wrote a piece about Robert Frank, the photographer and filmmaker.

sentences.en: Robert Frank made photographs that most people, when he took them, didn't consider beautiful, and some people were repelled by them.

sentences.en: He traveled around the country in the 1950s, taking many, many, many photographs.

sentences.en: And in those photographs, he tried to communicate the diversity of what made this country.

sentences.en: He tried to show how the United States was a country filled with all kinds of people.
sentences.zh: 他试图展示美国是一个充满了各种各样人的国家。

sentences.en: And he saw with such acuity, had such a perceptive eye, that his great ability was to help Americans to see themselves as they hadn't yet seen themselves.

sentences.en: After writing my piece, I stayed in touch with Robert Frank.

sentences.en: And I can tell you that the man who took such complex photographs was a complex person himself.

sentences.en: Last May, Robert Frank, the world's preeminent living photographer, returned to Zurich, the orderly Swiss banking city, cosseted by lake and mountain, where he grew up.
sentences.zh: 去年五月，世界上最杰出的在世摄影师罗伯特·弗兰克回到了他长大的地方——苏黎世，那座被湖泊和群山环抱、秩序井然的瑞士金融之城。

sentences.en: When an artist who made his reputation by leaving returns home, mixed feelings are inevitable.
sentences.zh: 当一位靠离开家乡而成名的艺术家重返故里时，复杂的情绪是不可避免的。

sentences.en: And that was especially true for Frank, whose iconic American pictures are notable for their deep understanding of human complication.
sentences.zh: 对于弗兰克来说尤其如此，他那标志性的美国照片以对人类复杂性的深刻理解而著称。

sentences.en: I know this town, but I certainly feel like a stranger here, he said.
sentences.zh: “我了解这座城市，但我在这里确实感觉像个陌生人，”他说。

sentences.en: As he walked through the immaculate Zurich city center with its many statues, gilded shop signs and fountains, Frank was just amazed how well organized everything is,
sentences.zh: 当他走在完美无瑕的苏黎世市中心，看着那众多的雕像、镀金的商店招牌和喷泉时，弗兰克对一切组织得如此井井有条感到惊讶，

sentences.en: how perfect everything is.
sentences.zh: 一切都如此完美。

sentences.en: The Swiss, he explained, do not throw coins into fountains, because they have everything they need.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，瑞士人不会往喷泉里扔硬币，因为他们拥有所需的一切。

sentences.en: They don't believe in wishing wells.
sentences.zh: 他们不相信许愿池。

sentences.en: Only the poor have to hope.

sentences.en: He said he never worried about being caught by inspectors, and he didn't seem worried.

sentences.en: He seemed the way he typically did, fully present and yet filled with personal mystery.
sentences.zh: 他看起来和他往常一样，完全沉浸在当下，却又充满了个人神秘感。

sentences.en: I don't know where that one goes, so we'll take it, he said, and was soon bound for a working-class district of the city.

sentences.en: He packed two cameras, many boxes of film, kept in a bag to protect them from the sun.
sentences.zh: 他带了两台相机，许多盒胶卷，装在袋子里以防阳光照射。

sentences.en: Trunks, French brandy.
sentences.zh: 行李箱，法国白兰地。

sentences.en: Sometimes you need a little drink.
sentences.zh: 有时候你需要喝上一小杯。

sentences.en: It changes your attitude.
sentences.zh: 它会改变你的态度。

sentences.en: AAA road atlases and one book, which was really a map of another kind, Evans's American photographs.
sentences.zh: 美国汽车协会的公路地图集和一本书，那其实是另一种地图，即埃文斯的《美国照片》。

sentences.en: Evans and others had suggested destinations like the Gullah communities of the South Atlantic coast, but Frank was often spontaneous.
sentences.zh: 埃文斯和其他人曾建议去南大西洋海岸的古拉社区等地，但弗兰克往往很随性。

sentences.en: The first destination was Michigan.
sentences.zh: 第一站是密歇根州。

sentences.en: I went to Detroit to photograph the Ford factories, and then it was clear to me I wanted to do this.
sentences.zh: 我去底特律拍摄福特工厂，那时我就清楚地知道我想做这件事。

sentences.en: It was summer and so loud, so much noise, so much heat.
sentences.zh: 那是夏天，声音很大，噪音很多，天气很热。

sentences.en: It was hell, so much screaming.
sentences.zh: 简直是地狱，尖叫声不断。

sentences.en: As Frank searched for pictures, he stayed in cheap motels.
sentences.zh: 当弗兰克寻找拍摄对象时，他住在廉价汽车旅馆里。

sentences.en: You'd always find them down by the river.
sentences.zh: 你总能在河边找到它们。

sentences.en: The first stop in a new town was usually a Woolworths department store.
sentences.zh: 到一个新城镇的第一站通常是伍尔沃斯百货商店。

sentences.en: His favorite shooting settings were public, sidewalks, political rallies, drive-ins, churches, parks.
sentences.zh: 他最喜欢的拍摄场景是公共场所、人行道、政治集会、免下车餐厅、教堂、公园。

sentences.en: He wanted to find the men and women others would consider unremarkable, as well as the symbols and objects that defined them.
sentences.zh: 他想寻找那些被他人视为平庸的男男女女，以及定义他们的符号和物体。

sentences.en: Falling into a place-to-place rhythm, he took pictures of bystanders, vagrants, newlyweds,
sentences.zh: 在从一个地方到另一个地方的节奏中，他拍摄了路人、流浪汉、新婚夫妇、

sentences.en: Christian crosses, jukeboxes, mailboxes, coffins, televisions, many cars, and those many flags.
sentences.zh: 基督教十字架、自动点唱机、邮箱、棺材、电视机、许多汽车，以及那些众多的旗帜。

sentences.en: It was an investigation, and in every frame there is pent-up atmosphere, pressure in the air, a sense of somebody's impending exposure, maybe Frank's.
sentences.zh: 这是一次调查，每一帧画面中都有压抑的氛围，空气中弥漫着压力，一种某人即将被曝光的感觉，也许是弗兰克自己。

sentences.en: Photography can reveal so much.
sentences.zh: 摄影可以揭示太多东西。

sentences.en: It's the invasion of the privacy of the people.
sentences.zh: 这是对人们隐私的侵犯。

sentences.en: Accordingly, there was an element of tradecraft.
sentences.zh: 因此，其中包含了一种行业技巧。

sentences.en: I felt like a detective or a spy.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己像个侦探或间谍。

sentences.en: Yes, often I had uncomfortable moments.
sentences.zh: 是的，我经常有不舒服的时刻。

sentences.en: Nobody gave me a hard time because I had a talent for not being noticed.
sentences.zh: 没人找我麻烦，因为我有不被注意的天赋。

sentences.en: He was neither tall nor short, did not appear to maintain regular relations with razors, scissors, or blankets, and dressed in a way that brought to mind the bottom of a suitcase.
sentences.zh: 他不高也不矮，似乎不常打理胡须、头发或衣物，穿着打扮让人想起行李箱底部的杂物。

sentences.en: I didn't change clothes too much.
sentences.zh: 我不怎么换衣服。

sentences.en: The Ford fit the man.
sentences.zh: 这辆福特车很适合他。

sentences.en: I loved that car.
sentences.zh: 我爱那辆车。

sentences.en: It was like any car, inconspicuous, he says.
sentences.zh: 它就像任何车一样，不显眼，他说。

sentences.en: I called it Loose, the only connection I ever had with Mr. Henry Loose.
sentences.zh: 我叫它“卢斯”，这是我和亨利·卢斯先生之间唯一的联系。

sentences.en: Years later, the photographer and curator,
sentences.zh: 多年后，摄影师兼策展人

sentences.en: Philip Brookman, learned just how committed Frank was to making pictures.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·布鲁克曼了解到了弗兰克对摄影的投入程度。

sentences.en: The two men were visiting Frank's troubled son Pablo on Thanksgiving at a psychiatric hospital.
sentences.zh: 感恩节那天，两人正在一家精神病院探望弗兰克陷入困境的儿子巴勃罗。

sentences.en: Many families were there.
sentences.zh: 许多家庭都在那里。

sentences.en: At one point, a patient sang a very clear and beautiful song she called,
sentences.zh: 有一次，一位病人唱了一首非常清晰动听的歌，她称之为

sentences.en: Sad Movie.
sentences.zh: 《悲伤电影》。

sentences.en: Brookman moved, crept his hand toward his camera, but he worried that taking a photo would be inappropriate.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克曼很感动，手伸向相机，但他担心拍照会不合时宜。

sentences.en: As the moment passed, he heard a familiar, gruff voice, You should have taken it.
sentences.zh: 当那一刻过去时，他听到一个熟悉的、粗哑的声音说：你应该拍下来的。

sentences.en: When Frank raised his camera and shot, the process was blurry quick, meaning he could capture what he saw as he perceived it.
sentences.zh: 当弗兰克举起相机拍摄时，过程模糊而迅速，这意味着他能捕捉到他所感知到的景象。

sentences.en: People, Frank says, don't like to be caught in private moments.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克说，人们不喜欢在私人时刻被拍到。

sentences.en: I think private moments make the interesting picture.
sentences.zh: 我认为私人时刻才能拍出有趣的照片。

sentences.en: It says something about Frank, that his favorite American's photograph shows the only people who caught him in the act.
sentences.zh: 这说明了弗兰克的一点，他最喜欢的美国照片展示了唯一拍到他正在拍摄过程中的人。

sentences.en: A black couple resting on the grass in a San Francisco park looks toward the lens in outrage.
sentences.zh: 一对黑人夫妇在旧金山公园的草地上休息，愤怒地看向镜头。

sentences.en: Beyond them are white city buildings.
sentences.zh: 在他们身后是白色的城市建筑。

sentences.en: What is conveyed is how it feels to be violated wherever you go.
sentences.zh: 所传达的是无论走到哪里都被侵犯的感觉。

sentences.en: Frank says he was most drawn to blacks.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克说他最被黑人所吸引。

sentences.en: The bare-chested boy in the back of a convertible.
sentences.zh: 敞篷车后座上赤裸上身的男孩。

sentences.en: The woman relaxing beside a field in sunny Carolina cotton country.
sentences.zh: 在阳光明媚的卡罗莱纳棉花地旁放松的女人。

sentences.en: The dignified men outside the funeral of a South Carolina undertaker, who uncannily bring to mind the day President Obama eulogized
sentences.zh: 南卡罗来纳州一位殡仪员葬礼外庄严的男人们，他们离奇地让人想起奥巴马总统致悼词的那一天

sentences.en: Clemente Pinckney.
sentences.zh: 克莱门特·平克尼。

sentences.en: At first, the South was to him very exotic, a life I knew nothing about.
sentences.zh: 起初，南方对他来说非常异域，那是我一无所知的生活。

sentences.en: Then, in November 1955, Frank was traversing the Arkansas side of the Mississippi River,
sentences.zh: 然后，在1955年11月，弗兰克正穿过密西西比河的阿肯色州一侧，

sentences.en: just whistling my song and driving on, as he says, when a patrol car pulled him over outside McGee.
sentences.zh: 正如他所说，正吹着口哨开着车，一辆巡逻车在麦基外把他拦了下来。

sentences.en: The policeman's report noted that Frank needed a bath and that subject talked with a foreign accent.
sentences.zh: 警察的报告指出，弗兰克需要洗澡，而且当事人说话带有外国口音。

sentences.en: Also suspicious were the contents of the car, cameras, foreign liquor.
sentences.zh: 车里的东西也很可疑，相机、外国酒。

sentences.en: Frank was on his way to photograph oil refineries in Louisiana.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克当时正要去拍摄路易斯安那州的炼油厂。

sentences.en: Are you a commie?
sentences.zh: 你是共产党吗？

sentences.en: He was asked.
sentences.zh: 有人这样问他。

sentences.en: Ten weeks earlier, Emmett Till was murdered a hundred miles away.
sentences.zh: 十周前，埃米特·蒂尔在百里之外被谋杀。

sentences.en: In Arkansas, Frank recalls, the cops pulled me in.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克回忆说，在阿肯色州，警察把我带走了。

sentences.en: They locked me in a cell.
sentences.zh: 他们把我关进牢房。

sentences.en: I thought,
sentences.zh: 我心想，

sentences.en: Jesus Christ, nobody knows I'm here.
sentences.zh: 天哪，没人知道我在这儿。

sentences.en: They can do anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么事都干得出来。

sentences.en: They were primitive.
sentences.zh: 他们太野蛮了。

sentences.en: Across the room, Frank could see a young black girl sitting there watching.
sentences.zh: 在房间对面，弗兰克看到一个年轻的黑人女孩坐在那儿看着他。

sentences.en: Very wonderful face.
sentences.zh: 那张脸真是太美了。

sentences.en: You see in her eyes, she's thinking, what are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 你从她的眼神里能看出，她在想：他们会对我做什么？

sentences.en: Because his camera had been confiscated, Frank considers the girl his missing Americans photograph.
sentences.zh: 因为相机被没收了，弗兰克把那个女孩视为他那组《美国人》摄影集中缺失的一张照片。

sentences.en: Around midnight, a policeman told Frank he had ten minutes to get across the river.
sentences.zh: 午夜时分，一名警察告诉弗兰克，他有十分钟时间离开，过河去。

sentences.en: That trip, I got to like black people so much more than white people.
sentences.zh: 那次旅行让我发现，我比喜欢白人更喜欢黑人。

sentences.en: Coming to America after growing up listening to tyranny on the radio, Frank had been foremost a grateful emigre, and early pictures suggested it.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克在听着收音机里的暴政广播中长大，来到美国后，他首先是一个心怀感激的移民，早期的照片也体现了这一点。

sentences.en: Now, through a lens, the country darkened, and Frank became, the photographer Eugene Richards says, a loaded gun.
sentences.zh: 如今，透过镜头，这个国家变得阴暗，正如摄影师尤金·理查兹所说，弗兰克成了一把上膛的枪。

sentences.en: Four days later in New Orleans, Frank photographed the line of faces looking through the trolley windows.
sentences.zh: 四天后，在纽奥良，弗兰克拍下了电车窗外那一排排面孔。

sentences.en: Once he saw that girl in McGee, he says, he knew what to look for.
sentences.zh: 他说，一旦他在麦基看到了那个女孩，他就知道自己该寻找什么了。

sentences.en: As he drove, Frank was in the grip flow of his imagination, finding pictures everywhere.
sentences.zh: 开车时，弗兰克沉浸在想象的洪流中，到处都能发现画面。

sentences.en: So many pictures that he now says of the period,
sentences.zh: 照片多到他现在谈起那段时期时说：

sentences.en: You don't have it that good all the time.
sentences.zh: 你不可能一直都那么幸运。

sentences.en: I was on the case.
sentences.zh: 我当时正全身心投入拍摄。

sentences.en: Occasional hitchhikers advised Frank where to go next, and spelled him behind the wheel while he
sentences.zh: 偶尔搭便车的路人会给弗兰克指路，并在他开车时替他分担，而他

sentences.en: slept in the back seat, or quietly raised up and snapped their pictures, as he did on US 91 outside
sentences.zh: 则在后座睡觉，或者悄悄起身抓拍他们的照片，就像他在爱达荷州布莱克福特外的91号公路上做的那样。

sentences.en: Blackfoot, Idaho.
sentences.zh: 布莱克福特，爱达荷州。

sentences.en: Sometimes he gave people rides, workers, prostitutes, but Frank did not seek personal connections.
sentences.zh: 有时他会载人，有工人、妓女，但弗兰克并不寻求建立私人联系。

sentences.en: The people in the Americans, I watched, he said, adding, I wanted to take the picture and walk away.
sentences.zh: 他说：我观察着《美国人》里的那些人，我只想拍下照片，然后走开。

sentences.en: One American's photograph came from a dimly lit New Mexico gut bucket.
sentences.zh: 其中一张《美国人》的照片来自新墨西哥州一家灯光昏暗的廉价酒吧。

sentences.en: It was a tough bar.
sentences.zh: 那是个很乱的酒吧。

sentences.en: You had to shoot from your hip.
sentences.zh: 你得随时准备抓拍。

sentences.en: In Elko, Nevada, Frank photographed the play at a gaming table.
sentences.zh: 在内华达州埃尔科，弗兰克拍下了赌桌上的博弈。

sentences.en: It's very seldom you get a picture of people gambling.
sentences.zh: 你很难拍到人们赌博的照片。

sentences.en: The management and the gamblers don't want you to take pictures because they have wives, or mothers, or grandmothers, or daughters.
sentences.zh: 管理人员和赌徒都不想让你拍照，因为他们有妻子、母亲、祖母或女儿。

sentences.en: At political gatherings, where credentials were required for admission, Frank was not above filching some from a stranger's jacket.
sentences.zh: 在需要凭证入场的政治集会上，弗兰克甚至会从陌生人的外套里顺手牵羊。

sentences.en: You could operate that way if you were on your own, but Frank was married, and those years were hard on the family.
sentences.zh: 如果你单枪匹马，或许能这么干，但弗兰克已经结婚了，那几年对家庭来说很艰难。

sentences.en: In photographs from the 1950s, the children are inevitably bright-eyed.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代的照片中，孩子们总是眼神明亮。

sentences.en: Mary is distantly aglow, and Frank Grimm.
sentences.zh: 玛丽显得有些疏离，而弗兰克则一脸严肃。

sentences.en: From the road, Frank wrote to Mary, your letters are often sad.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克在路上写信给玛丽说：你的信里总透着忧伤。

sentences.en: When they all met up in Texas and drove west for a few weeks,
sentences.zh: 当他们全家在德克萨斯州团聚并向西开车旅行了几周后，

sentences.en: Frank found it stressful.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克感到压力很大。

sentences.en: You go out.
sentences.zh: 你出门。

sentences.en: You're gone.
sentences.zh: 你离开了。

sentences.en: You come back.
sentences.zh: 你回来。

sentences.en: You're tired.
sentences.zh: 你累了。

sentences.en: You've hunted for pictures.
sentences.zh: 你一直在寻找画面。

sentences.en: You want peace.
sentences.zh: 你想要平静。

sentences.en: His family became the subject of his book's wistful last photograph.
sentences.zh: 他的家人成了他那本书最后一幅忧郁照片的主题。

sentences.en: Taken from in front of the car through the windshield, weary, overwhelmed faces and half the Ford are visible.
sentences.zh: 照片是从车前透过挡风玻璃拍的，可以看到疲惫、不知所措的面孔和半辆福特汽车。

sentences.en: It's personal.
sentences.zh: 这很私人。

sentences.en: It's melancholy.
sentences.zh: 这很忧郁。

sentences.en: It's sentimentality.
sentences.zh: 这很感伤。

sentences.en: All the things you try to stay away from.
sentences.zh: 所有你试图远离的东西。

sentences.en: Also,
sentences.zh: 还有，

sentences.en: I'm the person who's not there.
sentences.zh: 我是一个缺席的人。

sentences.en: This is what it takes, the picture says.
sentences.zh: 这张照片在说：这就是代价。

sentences.en: Frank took more than 27,000 photographs.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克拍了超过27000张照片。

sentences.en: Returning to New York, he sequenced the best 83 into what he thought of as a film on paper.
sentences.zh: 回到纽约后，他将其中最出色的83张编排成他心目中的“纸上电影”。

sentences.en: Walker Evans wrote him an introduction to help place it.
sentences.zh: 沃克·埃文斯为他写了一篇序言，以帮助定位这本书。

sentences.en: But who would publish images of groping teenagers, drifters, cross-dressers, poor blacks, a harassed mother?
sentences.zh: 但谁会出版那些关于摸索的青少年、流浪汉、异装癖者、贫穷的黑人和受骚扰的母亲的照片呢？

sentences.en: At first, only Robert Delpierre in Paris would.
sentences.zh: 起初，只有巴黎的罗伯特·德尔皮埃尔愿意。

sentences.en: Frank's inability to find an American publisher frustrated him.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克无法找到美国出版商，这让他感到沮丧。

sentences.en: He came to feel he needed a more like-minded advocate.
sentences.zh: 他开始觉得需要一个志同道合的拥护者。

sentences.en: So, Frank says, I turned to Kerouac.
sentences.zh: 所以，弗兰克说，我转向了凯鲁亚克。

sentences.en: It was early September 1957 when Frank heard about On the Road, a novel that had just been praised in the New York Times as the most important utterance yet made by the generation.
sentences.zh: 1957年9月初，弗兰克听说了《在路上》，这部小说刚在《纽约时报》上被誉为这一代人迄今为止最重要的宣言。

sentences.en: Frank liked the speed of it, taking you back and forth across the country, his descriptions of the landscape in the morning,
sentences.zh: 弗兰克喜欢它的节奏，带你往返于全国各地，他对清晨风景的描述，

sentences.en: the little towns, which he describes with such exquisite beauty, the love for America.
sentences.zh: 那些小镇，他描述得如此精致优美，还有对美国的热爱。

sentences.en: He found Kerouac at a New York party where poets and beatniks were, some painters.
sentences.zh: 他在纽约的一个聚会上找到了凯鲁亚克，那里有诗人和“垮掉派”，还有一些画家。

sentences.en: Everything happened downtown.
sentences.zh: 一切都发生在市中心。

sentences.en: When Frank showed the writer his pictures, Frank says he was empathetic.
sentences.zh: 当弗兰克向这位作家展示他的照片时，弗兰克说他很有共鸣。

sentences.en: Kerouac personified what I hoped I'd find here in America.
sentences.zh: 凯鲁亚克体现了我希望在美国找到的东西。

sentences.en: He was interested in outsiders.
sentences.zh: 他对局外人很感兴趣。

sentences.en: He wasn't interested in walking the middle of the road.
sentences.zh: 他没兴趣走寻常路。

sentences.en: Seizing the moment, Frank asked if Kerouac would introduce the Americans.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克抓住机会，问凯鲁亚克是否愿意为《美国人》写序。

sentences.en: Sure, Kerouac said.
sentences.zh: 当然，凯鲁亚克说。

sentences.en: I'll write something.
sentences.zh: 我会写点东西。

sentences.en: One reason many other artists believe, as Nan Golden says, that Frank has never taken a false step is that Frank always puts art above sentiment.
sentences.zh: 许多其他艺术家认为弗兰克从未走错一步，正如南·戈尔丁所说，原因之一是弗兰克总是把艺术置于情感之上。

sentences.en: I try to get out of sentiment's way when it comes near me.
sentences.zh: 当情感靠近我时，我尽量避开它。

sentences.en: A few steps backward and to the left and don't look back.
sentences.zh: 向后退几步，向左转，不要回头。

sentences.en: Frank says there was no hesitation about jilting Evans for Kerouac, but informing his mentor that he was forsaking him for Kerouac was a difficult moment.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克说，为了凯鲁亚克而抛弃埃文斯并没有什么犹豫，但通知他的导师自己要为了凯鲁亚克而离开他，那是一个艰难的时刻。

sentences.en: He says Evans' essay was too flowery and made no sense, adding, the friendship survived, but that was it.
sentences.zh: 他说埃文斯的文章太华丽，毫无意义，并补充道：友谊维持了下来，但仅此而已。

sentences.en: Never mentioned again.
sentences.zh: 再也没提过。

sentences.en: Their relationship became colder and more distant.
sentences.zh: 他们的关系变得更加冷淡和疏远。

sentences.en: Frank admired Kerouac's propulsive methods.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克钦佩凯鲁亚克那种推进式的创作方法。

sentences.en: He lay on the floor all evening long.
sentences.zh: 他整晚都躺在地板上。

sentences.en: He'd write 20 pages about it the next morning.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上他就能写出20页。

sentences.en: Introducing the Americans, Kerouac told a reader nothing about Frank's biography.
sentences.zh: 在为《美国人》作序时，凯鲁亚克只字未提弗兰克的生平。

sentences.en: Instead, he supplied an ecstasy of overture.
sentences.zh: 相反，他提供了一段狂喜的序曲。

sentences.en: With one hand, he sucked a sad poem of America onto film, taking rank among the tragic poets of the world.
sentences.zh: 他用一只手将一首关于美国的悲伤诗篇吸入胶片，跻身于世界悲剧诗人行列。

sentences.en: Yet the Americans was initially unappreciated in the United States.
sentences.zh: 然而，《美国人》最初在美国并不受赏识。

sentences.en: The editors of popular photography derided Frank's warped, wart-covered images of hate.
sentences.zh: 《大众摄影》的编辑们嘲笑弗兰克那些扭曲、布满“疣”的仇恨影像。

sentences.en: That the photographs were blurry, asymmetrical, shot at oblique angles, and deliberately informal, attracted more screeds.
sentences.zh: 照片模糊、不对称、以倾斜角度拍摄且刻意非正式，这些特点招致了更多的抨击。

sentences.en: The problem was, as the critic Janet Malcolm would later explain, no one had ever made pictures like that before.
sentences.zh: 正如评论家珍妮特·马尔科姆后来解释的那样，问题在于，以前从未有人拍过那样的照片。

sentences.en: At first, it was other American artists who were enthralled.
sentences.zh: 起初，是其他美国艺术家被深深吸引。

sentences.en: Out in Los Angeles, Ed Ruscha was sitting in an art student cafe when a classmate brought in a brand new copy of the book.
sentences.zh: 在洛杉矶，埃德·鲁沙正坐在艺术生咖啡馆里，一位同学拿来了一本崭新的书。

sentences.en: Suddenly, there weren't enough chairs for everyone.
sentences.zh: 突然间，椅子都不够坐了。

sentences.en: We were craning our necks, looking at it page by page.
sentences.zh: 我们伸长脖子，一页一页地看着。

sentences.en: It's like, you know where you were when John F.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道约翰·F·肯尼迪被枪杀时你在哪儿吗？

sentences.en: Kennedy was shot?
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪被枪杀时？

sentences.en: I know where I was when I saw the Americans.
sentences.zh: 我知道我看到《美国人》时我在哪儿。

sentences.en: For Ruscha, in Frank's hands, the camera became a new kind of machine.
sentences.zh: 对鲁沙来说，在弗兰克手中，相机变成了一种新型机器。

sentences.en: I was aware of Walker Evans' work, but I felt like those were still lives.
sentences.zh: 我知道沃克·埃文斯的作品，但我感觉那些是静物。

sentences.en: Robert's work was life in motion.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特的作品是运动中的生命。

sentences.en: Frank was not yet well-known, but he and Mary were a glamorous couple at the crossroads of the New York art scene.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克当时还不出名，但他和玛丽是纽约艺术圈十字路口的一对迷人夫妇。

sentences.en: He personally was a camera, a tough, sensual receptor with an enticing remove that made others draw near.
sentences.zh: 他本人就是一台相机，一个坚韧、感性的接收器，带着一种诱人的疏离感，吸引着别人靠近。

sentences.en: The people Frank admired were judgmental, unpredictable artists who satisfied his need for heightened experience.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克钦佩的人都是些爱评判、不可预测的艺术家，他们满足了他对极致体验的需求。

sentences.en: The jazz musician Ornette Coleman didn't like many things, a very hard critic.
sentences.zh: 爵士音乐家奥内特·科尔曼不喜欢很多东西，是个非常严苛的评论家。

sentences.en: While the filmmaker and musicologist Harry Smith lived to insult people, lit fires, yelled, hailed Hitler in Jewish restaurants, and yet was the only genius I ever met.
sentences.zh: 而电影制作人兼音乐学家哈里·史密斯活着就是为了侮辱人，放火、大喊大叫、在犹太餐馆里行纳粹礼，但他却是我见过唯一的奇才。

sentences.en: He was open to how people could reveal something for other people,
sentences.zh: 他乐于展现人们如何为他人揭示某些东西，

sentences.en: Frank says.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克说。

sentences.en: He lived uptown like a hermit, all alone, with all his windows closed.
sentences.zh: 他像个隐士一样住在上城，孤身一人，窗户紧闭。

sentences.en: Among photographers, Frank considered Diane Arbus a special woman.
sentences.zh: 在摄影师中，弗兰克认为黛安·阿勃丝是一位特别的女性。

sentences.en: I went to her house.
sentences.zh: 我去过她家。

sentences.en: She was eating something.
sentences.zh: 她正在吃东西。

sentences.en: She said, do you want some?
sentences.zh: 她说，你想吃点吗？

sentences.en: I said, sure.
sentences.zh: 我说，好啊。

sentences.en: I took a bite.
sentences.zh: 我咬了一口。

sentences.en: Almost impossible to eat.
sentences.zh: 简直难以下咽。

sentences.en: She said, yeah, I put too much salt in.
sentences.zh: 她说，是啊，我盐放多了。

sentences.en: She wanted to see my reaction.
sentences.zh: 她想看看我的反应。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: I liked her work.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢她的作品。

sentences.en: You could say, this is Diane Arbus.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，这就是黛安·阿勃丝。

sentences.en: Frank was closest to Ginsberg, Kerouac, and their circle, and says he was inspired by Ginsberg's relationship with the poet Peter Orlovsky.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克与金斯伯格、凯鲁亚克及其圈子关系最亲密，他说他受到了金斯伯格与诗人彼得·奥洛夫斯基关系的启发。

sentences.en: Of course, they were lovers, but he learned a lot about freedom from Orlovsky.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们是恋人，但他从奥洛夫斯基身上学到了很多关于自由的东西。

sentences.en: They could live on the edge of society, the edge of
sentences.zh: 他们可以生活在社会的边缘，生活在

sentences.en: American behavior.
sentences.zh: 美国行为的边缘。

sentences.en: They made me want to be freer.
sentences.zh: 他们让我想要变得更自由。

sentences.en: Frank would sit clothed in a room full of naked stone men, as Ginsberg read from poems like Kaddish.
sentences.zh: 当金斯伯格朗诵《卡迪什》之类的诗歌时，弗兰克会穿着衣服坐在满屋子赤裸的石像人中间。

sentences.en: It's wonderful to fall in with a group like that.
sentences.zh: 能加入这样一个群体真是太棒了。

sentences.en: You watch them live, and it's so different from what you'd seen.
sentences.zh: 你看着他们生活，那和你以前见过的完全不同。

sentences.en: Their art, their sexual lives, what truth they believed and preached and wrote.
sentences.zh: 他们的艺术、他们的性生活，他们相信、宣扬和书写的真理。

sentences.en: Ginsberg was a real prophet.
sentences.zh: 金斯伯格是一位真正的先知。

sentences.en: He saw a different, more accepting
sentences.zh: 他看到了一个不同、更具包容性的

sentences.en: America.
sentences.zh: 美国。

sentences.en: Frank once chauffeured Kerouac and his mother from Florida to Long Island.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克曾开车送凯鲁亚克和他的母亲从佛罗里达去长岛。

sentences.en: The author of On the Road Didn't Drive.
sentences.zh: 《在路上》的作者不会开车。

sentences.en: It's a better way to find out about the world if you don't.
sentences.zh: 如果你不会开车，这反而是了解世界更好的方式。

sentences.en: He was true talent.
sentences.zh: 他是个真正的天才。

sentences.en: He had a sad end.
sentences.zh: 他结局悲惨。

sentences.en: He couldn't handle his fame.
sentences.zh: 他无法应对自己的名声。

sentences.en: It drove him into a corner, made him drink, one to forget.
sentences.zh: 名声把他逼入死角，让他酗酒，为了遗忘。

sentences.en: Frank found closer personal understanding with James Agee than he did with Evans, Agee's collaborator on Let Us Now Praise Famous Men.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克与詹姆斯·阿吉的个人理解比与埃文斯（阿吉在《让我们赞美名人》中的合作者）更深。

sentences.en: And yet Agee, too, was always sweating and drinking, always a bottle close by.
sentences.zh: 然而阿吉也总是汗流浃背、酗酒，身边总放着酒瓶。

sentences.en: He was one of the saddest people I met, one of the suffering men.
sentences.zh: 他是我见过最悲伤的人之一，一个受苦的人。

sentences.en: When he wasn't interested in someone, Frank could be pitiless.
sentences.zh: 当弗兰克对某人不感兴趣时，他会变得冷酷无情。

sentences.en: I'm friendlier now.
sentences.zh: 我现在更友善了。

sentences.en: I had no patience.
sentences.zh: 我那时没有耐心。

sentences.en: He roiled with brutal standards.
sentences.zh: 他总是带着严苛的标准。

sentences.en: In Provincetown, a guy showed me his pictures and asked me what I thought.
sentences.zh: 在普罗温斯敦，有个家伙给我看他的照片，问我怎么看。

sentences.en: I tore them up.
sentences.zh: 我把它们撕了。

sentences.en: Now I hate myself for that.
sentences.zh: 现在我为此感到自责。

sentences.en: Then I had to.
sentences.zh: 当时我不得不这么做。

sentences.en: One day, the painter Mark Rothko invited Frank to his studio for a talk.
sentences.zh: 有一天，画家马克·罗斯科邀请弗兰克去他的工作室谈话。

sentences.en: It was a dark space with only a row of windows on the ceiling because, Frank says, Rothko liked the light to come in different colors.
sentences.zh: 那是一个昏暗的空间，天花板上只有一排窗户，因为弗兰克说，罗斯科喜欢光线以不同的颜色射入。

sentences.en: He had a daughter he worried about.
sentences.zh: 他有一个让他担心的女儿。

sentences.en: He asked for advice on young people.
sentences.zh: 他向弗兰克请教关于年轻人的建议。

sentences.en: I said I couldn't help him.
sentences.zh: 我说我帮不了他。

sentences.en: Being an artist, husband, and father continued to be arduous for Frank.
sentences.zh: 作为一名艺术家、丈夫和父亲，对弗兰克来说依然是艰巨的挑战。

sentences.en: During the 60s, he seemed tired, angry, and beaten down to friends like the filmmaker Jonas Mekas, who recalls Mary once stopping him on the street to ask if she
sentences.zh: 在60年代，在电影制作人乔纳斯·梅卡斯等朋友眼中，他显得疲惫、愤怒且备受打击，梅卡斯回忆起玛丽曾有一次在街上拦住他，问他

sentences.en: could borrow a dollar for groceries.
sentences.zh: 能不能借一美元买杂货。

sentences.en: The marriage struggled.
sentences.zh: 这段婚姻举步维艰。

sentences.en: But at the same time, Frank's achievement was slowly becoming understood, a momentum that continues.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，弗兰克的成就正逐渐被人们所理解，这种势头一直延续至今。

sentences.zh: 当今最优秀的摄影师，比如保罗·

sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆，仍然认为有人能将美国经验那无尽的奔涌塑造出一幅完整的国家肖像，这简直是启示性的。

sentences.en: Frank's book, Graham says, expresses a yearning in us all to find meaning and a pattern, a form to life.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆说，弗兰克的书表达了我们所有人内心的一种渴望：寻找意义、模式以及生活的形式。

sentences.en: Among the many qualities that enabled Frank to achieve something so ambitious was his profound ambivalence.
sentences.zh: 使弗兰克能够取得如此雄心勃勃成就的众多品质中，最重要的是他深刻的矛盾心理。

sentences.en: He was always that way personally, and it was how he could locate the full spectrum of any given feeling in the inscrutable faces of strangers.
sentences.zh: 他在个人生活中一直如此，也正是这种特质，让他能在陌生人那深不可测的面孔中捕捉到任何特定情感的完整光谱。

sentences.en: Critics like W.S.
sentences.zh: 像W.S.

sentences.en: DiPierro believe his genius for expressing emotional complication came from an artistic innocence,
sentences.zh: 迪皮耶罗这样的评论家认为，他表达情感复杂性的天才源于一种艺术上的天真，

sentences.en: the ability to look at the world as a child does, without the intrusions of experience.
sentences.zh: 即像孩子一样看待世界的能力，不受经验干扰的能力。

sentences.en: When June Leaf, Frank's wife of 40 years, discussed with me this way of her husband's seeing, she described being shown by his aunt a picture of Frank as a little boy.
sentences.zh: 当与弗兰克共同生活了40年的妻子琼·利夫与我谈论她丈夫这种观察方式时，她描述了弗兰克的姑姑曾给她看一张弗兰克小时候的照片。

sentences.en: I looked at it, and I thought to myself, that's exactly the same expression he has now.
sentences.zh: 我看着那张照片，心想，这和他现在的表情一模一样。

sentences.en: What is going on here?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: That's the secret of his perception of the world, and that's the Americans.
sentences.zh: 这就是他感知世界的秘密，也就是《美国人》的秘密。

sentences.en: That marvelous perception comes into the room.
sentences.zh: 那种奇妙的感知力进入了房间。

sentences.en: It's, what is going on here?
sentences.zh: 就是，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: None of us know until he takes a photograph.
sentences.zh: 在他按下快门之前，我们谁都不知道。

sentences.en: Other than the photograph, he doesn't know what is going on.
sentences.zh: 除了照片本身，他自己也不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: Over the years, the Americans would follow the trajectory of experimental American classics like
sentences.zh: 多年来，《美国人》遵循着像

sentences.zh: 《白鲸》和《公民凯恩》这类实验性美国经典作品的轨迹，这些作品的地位缓慢增长，直到仿佛它们一直就在那里一样。

sentences.en: To Bruce Springsteen, who keeps copies of The Americans Around His Home for songwriting motivation, the photographs are still shocking.
sentences.zh: 对于布鲁斯·斯普林斯汀来说，他家里一直放着《美国人》作为创作灵感，这些照片至今仍令人震撼。

sentences.en: It created an entire American identity, that single book.
sentences.zh: 那本书创造了整个美国身份认同。

sentences.en: To me, it's Dylan's Highway 61, the visual equivalent of that record.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它就像迪伦的《61号公路》专辑，是那张唱片的视觉对应物。

sentences.en: It's an 83-picture book that has 27,000 pictures in it.
sentences.zh: 那是一本收录了83张照片的书，里面却仿佛包含了27000张照片。

sentences.en: That's why Highway 61 is powerful.
sentences.zh: 这就是《61号公路》强大的原因。

sentences.en: It's nine songs with 12,000 songs in them.
sentences.zh: 那是九首歌，却仿佛包含了12000首歌。

sentences.en: We're all in the business of catching things.
sentences.zh: 我们都在从事捕捉事物的工作。

sentences.en: Sometimes we catch something.
sentences.zh: 有时我们能捕捉到一些东西。

sentences.en: He just caught all of it.
sentences.zh: 而他捕捉到了全部。

sentences.en: As the Americans thrived, Frank's success weighed on him.
sentences.zh: 随着《美国人》的成功，弗兰克感到了压力。

sentences.en: In the early 1970s, his friend, the photographer Edward Grazda, received a piece of mail from Frank written on a scrap of ledger paper.
sentences.zh: 1970年代初，他的朋友、摄影师爱德华·格拉兹达收到了一封弗兰克写在账本纸碎片上的信。

sentences.en: A postmark was the remote mining village in Nova Scotia where Frank and his new companion, Leaf, had escaped the admirers clamoring outside his New York door.
sentences.zh: 邮戳显示那是新斯科舍省一个偏远的矿业村庄，弗兰克和他的新伴侣利夫为了躲避纽约门外那些吵闹的仰慕者，逃到了那里。

sentences.en: That the man who made The Americans would leave photography was such a shocking decision that people in the arts still speculate about it.
sentences.zh: 那个创作了《美国人》的人竟然放弃了摄影，这个决定如此令人震惊，以至于艺术界至今仍在猜测原因。

sentences.en: He was painfully compassionate,
sentences.zh: “他有着令人心痛的同情心，”

sentences.zh: 彼得·谢尔达尔说。

sentences.en: Maybe he didn't want the pain anymore.
sentences.zh: “也许他不想再承受那种痛苦了。”

sentences.en: Frank put it this way in 1969.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克在1969年是这样说的。

sentences.en: Once respectability and success become a part of it, then it was time to look for a new mistress.
sentences.zh: “一旦受人尊敬和成功成为其中的一部分，那么就是时候寻找新的情妇了。”

sentences.en: He says now that the issue was creative fulfillment.
sentences.zh: 他现在说，问题在于创造性的满足感。

sentences.zh: “我不想重复自己。”

sentences.en: It's too easy.
sentences.zh: “那太容易了。”

sentences.zh: “这是一种挣扎，创作出好作品、满足自己是一种巨大的挣扎。”

sentences.zh: “这对我来说在摄影中相对容易。”

sentences.en: It's immediate recompense.
sentences.zh: “那是即时的回报。”

sentences.zh: 劳伦斯等文学叛逆者的美国出版商巴尼·罗塞特发行《美国人》时，弗兰克决定把我的莱卡相机放进柜子里，开始和住在市中心的邻居、画家阿尔弗雷德·莱斯利一起拍摄一部默片。

sentences.zh: 《拔掉我的雏菊》将凯鲁亚克未完成的剧本《垮掉的一代》中的一个场景，改编成了一个类似《宋飞正传》式的琐碎故事。

sentences.en: When Frank invited friends to a screening, he says, they were happy somebody looked at the world in a different way.

sentences.en: Across the next 40 years, Frank would release 31 mostly short, genre-eluding quasi-documentary movies that met with even less success than Pull My Daisy.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的40年里，弗兰克发行了31部大多是短片、难以归类的准纪录片，其成功程度甚至不及《拔掉我的雏菊》。

sentences.en: He says that working outside the studio system, operating completely against the rules of how you made a film, was challenging.
sentences.zh: 他说，在制片厂体系之外工作，完全违背电影制作规则去操作，是很有挑战性的。

sentences.en: And yet he filmed work that was, Jonas Mecca says, very important.
sentences.zh: 然而，乔纳斯·梅卡斯说，他拍摄的作品非常重要。

sentences.en: Same as Andy Warhol, he comes with his own world, his own sensibility, his own style.
sentences.zh: “就像安迪·沃霍尔一样，他带着自己的世界、自己的感性、自己的风格而来。”

sentences.en: The projects attracted a range of actors, Christopher Walken,

sentences.en: Frank's subjects were recondite, a book signing for a writer who never turns up, a day in the life of a country letter carrier.

sentences.en: Another, about indigenous American music, strayed and became a film about Frank.

sentences.en: Frank.

sentences.en: Frank also made a series of jagged, strangely absorbing personal films about friends and family

sentences.zh: 它们与之前的任何作品都如此不同，以至于它们共同构成了一股小型的纪录片浪潮。

sentences.zh: 其中三部是关于巴勃罗的，他是一个脆弱、受折磨的成年人，生活因精神分裂症而逐渐脱轨。

sentences.zh: 弗兰克解释说，他总是被极端的事物所吸引。

sentences.zh: “有好的一面，但我与另一半更有共鸣。”

sentences.en: And Julius, Frank felt, was on the edge of something.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克觉得，朱利叶斯正处于某种边缘。

sentences.en: I felt he would calm down and tell what it was like to be in this place.
sentences.zh: “我觉得他会平静下来，讲述身处那种境地是什么感觉。”

sentences.en: Frank considered his filmmaking career a failure, because often I don't want to reveal, but because it wasn't going well, it kept me going.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克认为他的电影生涯是失败的，因为“我经常不想揭露什么，但因为进展不顺，这反而让我坚持了下去”。

sentences.en: Defeat perversely encouraged Frank.
sentences.zh: 失败反而以一种反常的方式鼓励了弗兰克。

sentences.zh: 1972年，当时滚石乐队在洛杉矶完成他们的专辑《流亡主街》，邀请他为封面拍照。

sentences.en: The musician who most influenced Frank's work was Bob Dylan, who so frequently reinvented himself.
sentences.zh: 对弗兰克作品影响最大的音乐家是鲍勃·迪伦，他经常重塑自我。

sentences.en: Dylan has the talents to move on.
sentences.zh: 迪伦有继续前进的天赋。

sentences.en: But Keith Richards, Mick Jagger, and the rest of the Stones were the world's most celebrated outsiders, unregenerate avatars for collecting transgressive impulses into hits.
sentences.zh: 但基思·理查兹、米克·贾格尔和其他滚石成员是世界上最著名的局外人，是收集越轨冲动并将其转化为热门歌曲的顽固化身。

sentences.en: At a fleabag Los Angeles Inn, Frank recalls, they were instantly themselves.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克回忆说，在洛杉矶一家廉价旅馆里，他们瞬间就展现出了真实的自我。

sentences.en: Jagger said, let's rent a room.
sentences.zh: 贾格尔说，我们租个房间吧。

sentences.en: I sat them down in chairs and made them use hotel furniture.
sentences.zh: “我让他们坐在椅子上，让他们使用旅馆的家具。”

sentences.en: That's their life.
sentences.zh: “那就是他们的生活。”

sentences.en: Hotel rooMs. Hotel rooms and polish.
sentences.zh: “旅馆房间。旅馆房间和虚饰。”

sentences.zh: 超8摄像机同行。

sentences.en: Frank now says of the experience, I didn't care about the music.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克现在谈到那次经历时说：“我不在乎音乐。”

sentences.en: I cared about them.
sentences.zh: “我在乎的是他们。”

sentences.en: It was great to watch them, the excitement.
sentences.zh: “看着他们，那种兴奋感，真是太棒了。”

sentences.en: But my job was after the show.
sentences.zh: “但我的工作是在演出之后。”

sentences.en: What I was photographing was a kind of boredom.
sentences.zh: “我拍摄的是一种无聊。”

sentences.en: It's so difficult being famous.
sentences.zh: “出名太难了。”

sentences.en: It's a horrendous life.
sentences.zh: “那是一种可怕的生活。”

sentences.en: Everyone wants to get something from you.
sentences.zh: “每个人都想从你身上得到点什么。”

sentences.en: Frank showed Jagger a rough cut.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克给贾格尔看了粗剪版。

sentences.en: He looked at it, and then he said,
sentences.zh: 他看了一会儿，然后说，

sentences.zh: “理查兹比我拍得好。”

sentences.en: Robert made the better man win.
sentences.zh: “罗伯特让更好的人赢了。”

sentences.en: It's a very true documentation of what went down.
sentences.zh: “这是对所发生之事的非常真实的记录。”

sentences.en: The Stones' lawyers worried that the explicitness would create problems and forbade screening it unless Frank was in attendance.
sentences.zh: 滚石乐队的律师担心这种直白会引发问题，并禁止在弗兰克不在场的情况下放映该片。

sentences.en: As a result, the all but unavailable Blues is a celluloid apparition.
sentences.zh: 结果，几乎无法看到的《布鲁斯》成了一个胶片幽灵。

sentences.zh: 小说家唐·德里罗看过一个廉价的盗版拷贝。

sentences.en: He'd admired Frank's photographs for the way they imply a story or a sociology.
sentences.zh: 他一直钦佩弗兰克的照片，因为它们暗示了一个故事或一种社会学意义。

sentences.en: But the film,
sentences.zh: 但这部电影，

sentences.zh: “有一种纯粹的东西。”

sentences.en: In DeLillo's underworld, as characters view the film, DeLillo describes at length its crepuscular, edge-of-time feeling.
sentences.zh: 在德里罗的《地下世界》中，当角色观看这部电影时，德里罗详细描述了那种黄昏般的、处于时间边缘的感觉。

sentences.en: Since the 1970s, Frank's subversive approach has made him a godfather to young filmmakers.
sentences.zh: 自1970年代以来，弗兰克的颠覆性方法使他成为了年轻电影制作人的教父。

sentences.en: The strength of his films is in what he says is problematic, Jim Jarmusch says.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·贾木许说，他电影的力量在于他所说的那些充满争议的东西。

sentences.en: The beauty is they don't satisfy certain narrative conventions.
sentences.zh: 美妙之处在于，它们并不满足于某些叙事惯例。

sentences.en: Out in Texas in 1995, Richard Linklater was just beginning his film career when he staged a Frank retrospective at a theater in Austin.
sentences.zh: 1995年，理查德·林克莱特在德克萨斯州刚开始他的电影生涯，当时他在奥斯汀的一家剧院举办了一场弗兰克的作品回顾展。

sentences.en: If Robert Frank weren't so acclaimed as one of the most influential photographers of all time, he'd have a much larger profile as an American indie filmmaking icon, Linklater says.
sentences.zh: 林克莱特说，如果罗伯特·弗兰克不是作为史上最有影响力的摄影师之一而广受赞誉，他作为美国独立电影偶像的形象会更加高大。

sentences.en: It seems our culture struggles with the idea that someone could be that groundbreaking in more than one area.
sentences.zh: 我们的文化似乎很难接受一个人能在多个领域都如此具有开创性。

sentences.en: If it were just the films, I think he'd be credited as a founding father of the personal film, he adds.
sentences.zh: 他补充道，如果仅仅是电影，我想他会被公认为个人电影的奠基人。

sentences.en: Beyond that, there's this tremendous range of a restless, searching artist pushing the boundaries of the documentary, experimental, and more traditional narrative

sentences.zh: 在纽约感到不堪重负、渴望平静的弗兰克，请求利夫去新斯科舍省的布雷顿角为他们找个家。

sentences.en: He became a sweet father to Pablo, where before he'd been explosive.
sentences.zh: 他成了巴勃罗温柔的父亲，而在此之前，他一直是个暴躁的人。

sentences.en: Very critical, dictatorial, authoritarian, like many European fathers.
sentences.zh: “非常挑剔、独裁、专制，就像许多欧洲父亲一样。”

sentences.en: Pablo was so ethereal, funny, charming, sweet.
sentences.zh: 巴勃罗是那么空灵、有趣、迷人、甜美。

sentences.en: The illness made Robert a better father.
sentences.zh: 疾病让罗伯特成为了一个更好的父亲。

sentences.en: He had to be.
sentences.zh: 他不得不如此。

sentences.en: For many years after leaving New York, Frank remained relentlessly productive.
sentences.zh: 离开纽约后的许多年里，弗兰克始终保持着不懈的创作力。

sentences.en: He made films and resumed taking photographs, personal images of a very different style from street photography.
sentences.zh: 他拍摄电影并重新开始摄影，这些个人影像与街头摄影风格迥异。

sentences.en: In 1972, a Japanese first-time publisher named Kazuhiko Motamura collaborated with Frank on The Lines of My Hand.
sentences.zh: 1972年，一位名叫本村和彦的日本出版商首次与弗兰克合作出版了《我手的线条》。

sentences.en: An expanded American edition was published in 1989 and became a book crucial to American photographers.
sentences.zh: 1989年出版的扩充版美国版成为了美国摄影师至关重要的一本书。

sentences.en: Jim Goldberg describes it as,
sentences.zh: 吉姆·戈德堡将其描述为：

sentences.en: A Roadmap for the Rest of My Hand.
sentences.zh: “我手的余生路线图。”

sentences.en: Many of the most powerful pictures are of Pablo, his face ravaged by illness.
sentences.zh: 许多最有力量的照片都是关于巴勃罗的，他的脸被疾病摧残。

sentences.en: Photographs are distressed, dripping with tears of paint, writhed with scratched-out messages.
sentences.zh: 照片显得支离破碎，滴着油漆的泪水，扭曲着被划掉的信息。

sentences.en: Of his son, Frank writes, What a hard life we have together.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克在写到儿子时说：“我们在一起的生活多么艰难。”

sentences.en: I can't take it.
sentences.zh: “我受不了了。”

sentences.en: In and out of institutions, Pablo committed suicide in 1994.
sentences.zh: 在多次进出精神病院后，巴勃罗于1994年自杀身亡。

sentences.en: Robert was always attracted to mad people like Julius Orlovsky, Leaf says, because he had nothing of that in him.
sentences.zh: 利夫说，罗伯特总是被像朱利叶斯·奥洛夫斯基这样的疯子所吸引，因为他自己身上完全没有那种特质。

sentences.en: So it's fate, isn't it, Pablo?
sentences.zh: “所以这是命，对吧，巴勃罗？”

sentences.en: Eventually, Frank gave in to grief.
sentences.zh: 最终，弗兰克屈服于悲伤。

sentences.en: It takes concentration for me to work, and the wish to succeed, Frank says.
sentences.zh: “我工作需要专注，还需要成功的愿望，”弗兰克说。

sentences.en: I didn't have it anymore.
sentences.zh: “我再也没有这些了。”

sentences.en: With such loss, he said, you have to cope every day, and it doesn't go away.
sentences.zh: 他说，面对这样的损失，你必须每天应对，而且这种痛苦不会消失。

sentences.en: You try hard to find some peace and acceptance.
sentences.zh: 你努力去寻找一些平静和接受。

sentences.en: Frank dislikes talking about any of it.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克不喜欢谈论这一切。

sentences.en: It's not good to look back too much.
sentences.zh: “回顾太多并不好。”

sentences.en: It's often sad.
sentences.zh: “这通常很悲伤。”

sentences.en: Better to look forward.
sentences.zh: “向前看更好。”

sentences.en: I felt I should ask him about Leaf's descriptions of his children.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我应该问问他关于利夫对他孩子们的描述。

sentences.en: He didn't disagree with anything she'd said.
sentences.zh: 他并没有反驳她所说的任何话。

sentences.en: Then he sighed.
sentences.zh: 然后他叹了口气。

sentences.en: I could have helped him.
sentences.zh: “我本可以帮他的。”

sentences.en: He would have needed another family, a real mother, a real father, to take care of him.
sentences.zh: “他需要另一个家庭，一个真正的母亲，一个真正的父亲来照顾他。”

sentences.en: I think about that too often, because it's too late.
sentences.zh: “我太频繁地想到这一点，因为已经太晚了。”

sentences.en: Frank and Leaf now live most of the year in a building off the Bowery that has open hearths and rough surfaces and feels like a vertical farmhouse, a Manhattan version of Mabu.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和利夫现在一年中的大部分时间都住在鲍厄里街附近的一栋建筑里，那里有开放的壁炉和粗糙的表面，感觉就像一个垂直的农舍，是马布的曼哈顿版本。

sentences.en: In a neighborhood now awash in tiny boats and boutiques, Frank and Leaf are remnants of vanished bohemian New York.
sentences.zh: 在这个如今充斥着小船和精品店的街区，弗兰克和利夫是消失的波西米亚纽约的遗存。

sentences.en: In Frank's musty basement studio, amid a jumble of contact sheets, Camus novels, toy crocodiles, and checkerboards, Eat is scrawled on the wall in yellow.
sentences.zh: 在弗兰克发霉的地下室工作室里，在一堆接触印样、加缪小说、玩具鳄鱼和棋盘中，墙上用黄色潦草地写着“吃”。

sentences.en: Patty Smith wrote that, he says.
sentences.zh: “那是帕蒂·史密斯写的，”他说。

sentences.en: Visitors are always stopping by.
sentences.zh: 访客总是络绎不绝。

sentences.en: Leaf receives them bright-eyed.
sentences.zh: 利夫总是目光炯炯地接待他们。

sentences.en: I'm a bouncy.
sentences.zh: “我是一个充满活力的人。”

sentences.en: Frank watches warily, but with an eyebrow raised.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克警惕地看着，但挑起了一边眉毛。

sentences.en: He's always waiting for something extraordinary, Leaf says.
sentences.zh: “他总是在等待某种非凡的事情，”利夫说。

sentences.en: Frank and Leaf married in 1975 while passing through Reno, Nevada, an echo to the eloping couple in The Americans.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和利夫于1975年在途经内华达州里诺市时结婚，这与《美国人》中私奔的情侣遥相呼应。

sentences.en: Over the years, Leaf has developed what she calls a bad habit of studying Robert.
sentences.zh: 多年来，利夫养成了一种她称之为“研究罗伯特”的坏习惯。

sentences.en: Once she asked me, do you think Robert's elusive?
sentences.zh: 有一次她问我：“你觉得罗伯特难以捉摸吗？”

sentences.en: Instead, Frank answered, I used to be.
sentences.zh: 相反，弗兰克回答说：“我曾经是。”

sentences.en: I didn't like to explain anything.
sentences.zh: “我不喜欢解释任何事情。”

sentences.en: You still don't, she said, and you don't like things to be explained, and I'm a great explainer.
sentences.zh: “你现在依然不喜欢，”她说，“而且你不喜欢事情被解释，而我是一个伟大的解释者。”

sentences.en: It's a miracle we lasted this long.
sentences.zh: “我们能维持这么久真是个奇迹。”

sentences.en: At 85, Leaf has a grave mystical face that resembles Georgia O'Keeffe's.
sentences.zh: 85岁的利夫有着一张庄重而神秘的脸，酷似乔治亚·欧姬芙。

sentences.en: She sees her husband clearly.
sentences.zh: 她清楚地看透了自己的丈夫。

sentences.en: You have no idea how mean Robert can be.
sentences.zh: “你根本不知道罗伯特可以有多刻薄。”

sentences.en: And with delight.
sentences.zh: 而且是带着愉悦感。

sentences.en: In Philip Brookman's 1986 documentary on Frank, Fire in the East, Leaf says, He goes through life in this wonderful, secret way, in the water, under the water.
sentences.zh: 在菲利普·布鲁克曼1986年拍摄的关于弗兰克的纪录片《东方之火》中，利夫说：“他以这种美妙、隐秘的方式度过一生，在水中，在水下。”

sentences.en: And things just come to him.
sentences.zh: “而事情就这样自然而然地来到他身边。”

sentences.en: So he's like a fish, a beautiful fish in the dark, lighting up the water.
sentences.zh: “所以他就像一条鱼，一条黑暗中美丽的鱼，照亮了水面。”

sentences.en: Although Frank still retains a certain Swiss civility, he enjoys provocation in others.
sentences.zh: 尽管弗兰克仍然保持着某种瑞士式的礼貌，但他喜欢挑衅他人。

sentences.en: He refers to the French celebrity photographer François-Marie Bagnier, notorious for insinuating himself into the affections of wealthy older women, as the bad man friend of mine.
sentences.zh: 他称那位以钻营富有的年长女性的感情而臭名昭著的法国名人摄影师弗朗索瓦-玛丽·巴尼耶为“我那个坏蛋朋友”。

sentences.en: On stage at Lincoln Center, when his chosen interviewer, Charlie LeDuff, asked about the state of Frank's rectum, Frank was amused at the general mortification.
sentences.zh: 在林肯中心的舞台上，当他指定的采访者查理·勒达夫问及弗兰克的直肠状况时，弗兰克对这种普遍的尴尬感到好笑。

sentences.en: Some days Frank is a steel door.
sentences.zh: 有时弗兰克是一扇钢铁大门。

sentences.en: Others, he is impish, a trickster.
sentences.zh: 有时，他又像个顽童，是个恶作剧者。

sentences.en: Not long after he renounced his Leica, word circulated among other photographers that he was entering photo contests under assumed names in winning.
sentences.zh: 在他放弃徕卡相机后不久，摄影界就传言他正以化名参加摄影比赛并获奖。

sentences.en: Ask him how he is, and Frank may reply, 50%.
sentences.zh: 问他近况如何，弗兰克可能会回答：“50%。”

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: “那是什么意思？”

sentences.en: If it goes below 50%, my red light goes on.
sentences.zh: “如果低于50%，我的红灯就会亮起。”

sentences.en: One day, he loves crowds.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他热爱人群。

sentences.en: Another day, crowds are impossible.
sentences.zh: 另一天，人群又变得无法忍受。

sentences.en: A third pass, and the dark eyes gleam, and there's nothing like a medium-sized crowd.
sentences.zh: 再过一阵，那双黑眼睛闪烁着光芒，又觉得中等规模的人群再好不过了。

sentences.en: His terse style of speaking sometimes produces epigraMs. It's the misinformation that's important.
sentences.zh: 他简洁的说话风格有时会产生警句。“重要的反而是那些错误信息。”

sentences.en: Take that seriously, warns Brookman, who has known Frank since the 1970s.
sentences.zh: “要认真对待这一点，”布鲁克曼警告说，他从1970年代就认识弗兰克了。

sentences.en: He loves misleading people.
sentences.zh: “他喜欢误导别人。”

sentences.en: When Frank is feeling affectionate, his puckish banter is seductive to younger artists, especially photographers.
sentences.zh: 当弗兰克感到亲切时，他那顽皮的玩笑对年轻艺术家，尤其是摄影师来说，极具诱惑力。

sentences.en: Many men have felt for a time like a second son to Frank, only to abruptly find that some sort of personal fission has occurred.
sentences.zh: 许多男人曾一度觉得自己像是弗兰克的第二个儿子，却突然发现某种个人裂变发生了。

sentences.en: The focus of Frank's guarded eyes has moved on, and they've been purged.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克那警惕的目光已经转移，而他们已被清除。

sentences.en: His longtime gallerist, Peter McGill, has grown accustomed to offering consolation.
sentences.zh: 他长期的画廊主彼得·麦吉尔已经习惯了提供安慰。

sentences.en: Robert hurts the people he's closest to.
sentences.zh: “罗伯特会伤害他最亲近的人。”

sentences.en: One photographer, in an anticipatory gambit, stopped talking with Frank for more than two years.
sentences.zh: 一位摄影师为了先发制人，停止与弗兰克交谈超过两年。

sentences.en: When I met McGill, he warned me, everybody who knows him gets periodically fired.
sentences.zh: 当我见到麦吉尔时，他警告我：“每个认识他的人都会定期被解雇。”

sentences.en: It's not that you're not a contestant anymore for something extraordinary, Leif says.
sentences.zh: “这并不是说你不再是某种非凡事物的竞争者了，”利夫说。

sentences.en: We all fall short.
sentences.zh: “我们都做得不够好。”

sentences.en: It's the way a man desires a woman.
sentences.zh: “这就是男人渴望女人的方式。”

sentences.en: This is the one.
sentences.zh: “就是这个人了。”

sentences.en: He's always hoping somebody will change the view of the world.
sentences.zh: 他总是希望有人能改变这个世界观。

sentences.en: The personal quality Frank perhaps values most is autonomy, and when others want too much from him, he gets prickly and feels exploited.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克或许最看重的个人品质是自主性，当别人对他要求过多时，他会变得敏感并感到被利用。

sentences.en: It's time to leave.
sentences.zh: “是时候离开了。”

sentences.en: It was always important to him to remain independent of Switzerland, his family, Life Magazine,
sentences.zh: 对他来说，保持独立于瑞士、他的家庭、《生活》杂志、

sentences.en: Cartier-Bresson, Evans, and go forward.
sentences.zh: 布列松、埃文斯，并继续前进，这始终很重要。

sentences.en: Keep pushing, Brookman says.
sentences.zh: “继续推动，”布鲁克曼说。

sentences.en: There have been unbroken bonds.
sentences.zh: 也有一些从未断裂的纽带。

sentences.en: Sarah Green, our senior curator of photographs at the National
sentences.zh: 国家美术馆摄影部高级策展人莎拉·格林

sentences.en: Gallery, says Frank and Motomura always were devoted, even though Robert didn't speak Japanese and Motomura didn't speak English.
sentences.zh: 说，弗兰克和本村一直很忠诚，尽管罗伯特不会说日语，而本村也不会说英语。

sentences.en: Another person on whom the door has never closed is Peter Kasovitz, the gregarious owner of K&M Camera in New York.
sentences.zh: 另一个从未被他拒之门外的人是彼得·卡索维茨，纽约K&M相机店那位热情好客的老板。

sentences.en: Many in Frank's community wonder why Kasovitz should be spared.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克圈子里的许多人都想知道为什么卡索维茨能幸免。

sentences.en: Frank, whose father sold electronics, says Kasovitz is the consummate independent operator.
sentences.zh: 父亲从事电子产品销售的弗兰克说，卡索维茨是完美的独立经营者。

sentences.en: He doesn't go by others' rules.
sentences.zh: “他不按别人的规则行事。”

sentences.en: He just runs things in a way he believes.
sentences.zh: “他只是按照他相信的方式经营事情。”

sentences.en: For decades, Frank refused honors and exhibitions.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，弗兰克拒绝了各种荣誉和展览。

sentences.en: He once skipped a private celebration for the Museum of Modern Art's new photography curator because he wanted to test the set of tires he'd just acquired for his Subaru.
sentences.zh: 他曾缺席现代艺术博物馆新任摄影策展人的私人庆祝活动，因为他想测试一下他刚为斯巴鲁汽车换上的那套轮胎。

sentences.en: But lately, he attends his openings.
sentences.zh: 但最近，他开始出席自己的开幕式了。

sentences.en: This summer, he accepted an honorary degree from the Nova Scotia College of Art and Design.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，他接受了新斯科舍艺术与设计学院颁发的荣誉学位。

sentences.en: Frank retains the spontaneous enthusiasm of a much younger man.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克依然保持着年轻人那种自发的激情。

sentences.en: In his tenth decade, he is still a free-form outsider seeking untried situations, fresh leaps, and nothing pleases him more than picking up on the scent of something exceptional.
sentences.zh: 在他九十多岁时，他仍然是一个寻求未尝试过的情况、新鲜飞跃的自由形式局外人，没有什么比嗅到非凡事物的气息更让他高兴的了。

sentences.en: Last year, after receiving intriguing letters postmarked North Carolina from an itinerant laborer named Gustavo, Frank set off to find him.
sentences.zh: 去年，在收到来自北卡罗来纳州、邮戳上写着一个名叫古斯塔沃的流动工人的有趣信件后，弗兰克出发去寻找他。

sentences.en: He discovered Gustavo in Winston-Salem painting a house, he says, but I was disappointed in him.
sentences.zh: 他在温斯顿-塞勒姆发现了正在粉刷房子的古斯塔沃，他说：“但我对他感到失望。”

sentences.en: He was ordinary.
sentences.zh: “他很普通。”

sentences.en: He seemed not to be possessed by anything.
sentences.zh: “他似乎没有被任何东西所占据。”

sentences.en: He just drifts.
sentences.zh: “他只是随波逐流。”

sentences.en: A more satisfactory result came after an unannounced knock on the door from a
sentences.zh: 一个更令人满意的结果，源于一次不速之客的敲门，

sentences.en: California family.
sentences.zh: 那是一个来自加州的家庭。

sentences.en: The father, Leif says, was a junk collector looking for a masterpiece.
sentences.zh: 莱夫说，那位父亲是个专门寻找杰作的旧货收藏者。

sentences.en: Recently, he'd purchased three pictures.
sentences.zh: 最近，他买下了三幅画。

sentences.en: One looked like it was from Woolworths, and he thought it was a Boucher.
sentences.zh: 其中一幅看起来像是从伍尔沃斯百货买的廉价货，但他却以为那是布歇的作品。

sentences.en: The second was the worst thing you ever saw.
sentences.zh: 第二幅画是你见过最糟糕的东西。

sentences.en: He thought it was a de Kooning.
sentences.zh: 他却以为那是德·库宁的作品。

sentences.en: The third, somebody tells him it's a Tsanyo.
sentences.zh: 至于第三幅，有人告诉他那是桑约的作品。

sentences.en: He looks it up and sees Robert knows him.
sentences.zh: 他查了一下，发现罗伯特认识这位画家。

sentences.en: So the family crossed the country by car to show Frank the painting, possibly by Tsanyo.
sentences.zh: 于是，这家人开车横跨全国，来向弗兰克展示这幅可能是桑约画作的作品。

sentences.en: You don't have to open your eyes to see it's not a Tsanyo painting, Leif says.
sentences.zh: 莱夫说，你根本不用睁眼就能看出那不是桑约的画。

sentences.en: He doesn't mind.
sentences.zh: 但他并不介意。

sentences.en: He's a speculator.
sentences.zh: 他是个投机者。

sentences.en: He's happy.
sentences.zh: 他很开心。

sentences.en: Eventually,
sentences.zh: 最终，

sentences.en: Leif and Frank had to go out.
sentences.zh: 莱夫和弗兰克不得不出门。

sentences.en: What do you want to do?
sentences.zh: 你们想做什么？

sentences.en: Leif asked their visitors.
sentences.zh: 莱夫问他们的访客。

sentences.en: Nothing, came the answer.
sentences.zh: 什么也不做，对方回答道。

sentences.en: We came to see you.
sentences.zh: 我们就是来看你们的。

sentences.en: The family made their hosts tortillas from scratch and drove off for
sentences.zh: 这家人亲手为主人做了玉米饼，然后开车前往

sentences.en: Louisiana to surprise an aunt.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州去给一位姑妈制造惊喜。

sentences.en: Frank found all of this immensely satisfying.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克觉得这一切都极其令人满足。

sentences.en: I liked his directness, completely direct.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他的直接，完全的直接。

sentences.en: I could tell them about Tsanyo.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉他们关于桑约的事。

sentences.en: They had no interest in June or in my photographs.
sentences.zh: 他们对琼或者我的摄影作品毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: And so Frank decided that the father should have his masterpiece after all.
sentences.zh: 于是弗兰克决定，无论如何，这位父亲理应得到他的杰作。

sentences.en: I sent them two of my photographs.
sentences.zh: 我寄给了他们两张我的摄影作品。

sentences.en: I wonder if they found out what people pay for a print like that.
sentences.zh: 不知道他们有没有发现人们为了这样一张照片会付多少钱。

sentences.en: This was recorded by
sentences.zh: 本节目由

sentences.en: Autumn.
sentences.zh: Autumn录制。

sentences.zh: Autumn是一款你可以下载的应用程序，用来收听来自诸如

sentences.en: New York Times.

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。
